alt: The repair café email task decoded with four questions: the purpose is to persuade and request support; the audience is the head of school, so the register is formal; the text type is an email with a subject line, greeting, paragraphs, request and sign-off; the stimulus gives free repairs, volunteers, everyday objects, 40 items saved and images of shared work and less waste.
caption: Purpose, audience, text type and stimulus decide everything you write next.

alt: An email plan in five parts: an opening that states why you are writing, paragraph 1 explaining the idea, paragraph 2 giving reasons, paragraph 3 answering an objection about cost and safety, and a close that makes the request. Answering an objection shows awareness of the reader.
caption: Give every paragraph one job; answer the reader’s likely doubt.

alt: Four short separate sentences about the café are rewritten with the same ideas linked by “because”, “this”, “also”, “furthermore” and “so”. Below, connectives grouped by function: adding, contrasting, result, example and sequencing. A connective must match the logic of the ideas it joins.
caption: Connectives and reference words show how ideas relate.

alt: One idea at three points on a scale from informal to formal: a message to a friend, a school newsletter line and a formal proposal to the head. A table contrasts informal and formal greetings, forms of address, contractions, vocabulary and sentences. Register drift, such as a formal email ending “Anyway, let me know, thanks!”, is the commonest error.
caption: Choose the register when you decode the task, then keep it in every paragraph.

alt: Rising columns show the range to aim for: emergent, short accurate sentences with basic connectives; capable, reasons, more than one time frame and some complex sentences; proficient, precise word choice, varied structures and natural idiom. Then a checking order: verbs, agreement, word order, spelling and accents, and register, plus a personal error list.
caption: Stretch your range only as far as you can keep it accurate.

alt: Extracts from the model email to the head of school, each annotated: a subject line; a formal greeting with the purpose stated; a past-tense paragraph reusing ideas from the poster; sequencing connectives and a reference word using the poster image; a paragraph answering an objection with “however”; and a polite request with a formal sign-off.
caption: Each paragraph has one job, the ideas are linked, and the register stays formal.
